items.title: Google ships the Gemini API CLI (beta): a stateless command-line client built for agent subprocesses, scripts and CI
items.summary: New `gemini-api` CLI (beta, Oct 27): "a stateless, zero-dependency command-line client built for AI agents with shell access" that uses the Interactions API to generate text and media, analyze files, and run Gemini-managed agents — run the same commands from an agent subprocess, your terminal, or a CI pipeline.
items.why: A CLI meant to be called by other agents and CI jobs, not typed by a human, is a different design point than a chat client.
items.action: If a CI pipeline or agent harness step currently shells out to curl for a Gemini call, swap it for one gemini-api command and compare.

items.summary: "This one 'step' has improved the quality of tests more than any prompt tweak I have tried. items.title: SENTINEL: a six-agent system that argues about a production failure before it's allowed to fix it
items.summary: Mission Controller, Codebase Analyst, Failure Hypothesis, Root-Cause, Repair, and a separate Adversarial Verification agent whose only job is to break the proposed fix before it ships. Every step is gated by confidence scores; an unsure system escalates to a human. Includes a live interactive demo replaying three production incidents, plus full source.
items.why: "In agent systems, the engineering is in the brakes" — a concrete, inspectable pattern for knowing when an autonomous fix should NOT ship.
items.action: Open the live demo and watch how the Adversarial Verification agent's rejection path works, then check whether your own agent harness has an equivalent step.

eval.reason: Specific multi-agent architecture with a working demo and code, not a conceptual teardown; not a duplicate.

items.title: LangChain benchmarked 7 browser toolsets for Deep Agents and switched to Stagehand — with real numbers
items.summary: On WebVoyager (100 tasks, Claude Sonnet 5.5), Stagehand hit a 90% pass rate for $1.98 total vs. Playwright MCP's 78% for $26.71 (13x the cost, ~3x the time). Batching browser steps into one call ('code mode') cut cost another 4x; a wait-condition fix cut median task time from 182s to 124s with no accuracy loss. Ships as StagehandMiddleware in langchain-stagehand.
items.why: Browser-driven testing and verification is exactly the long, turn-heavy workload coding agents choke on — this is a benchmarked fix, not a vendor claim.
items.action: If your agent harness drives a browser to test or verify what it built, swap in StagehandMiddleware on one workflow and re-run your own evals before and after.

eval.reason: Real benchmark numbers and a shipped middleware, not a bare version-bump line; not a duplicate.
